To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) topic knowledge and cognitive interest are positively correlated; (b) the relationship between topic knowledge and cognitive is stronger than the relationship between text recall and cognitive interest; (c) readers who know nothing are more likely to be bored than fascinated, readers who know everything are more likely to find the text boring than fascinating, and readers who know something are more likely to enjoy the text than find it boring; and (d) readers who know something about a topic are more likely to recall text
the more a reader knew about the topic of a text, the more he/she was likely to recall from the text, and the more he/she recalled from the text, the more interested he/she was in the text.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of interest in learning.
the cognitive processes involved in learning from texts.
the role of prior knowledge in text processing and learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
topic knowledge is a necessary but not sufficient condition for generating cognitive interest in text.
topic knowledge is an important variable for the development of cognitive interest in descriptive texts.
the more one knows about the topic, the more one will learn.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the more a reader knows about a text, the more he or she will be interested in the text.
cognitive interest is not determined by how much the reader knows about the subject of the text, but by how much he or she knows about the subject that is presented in the text.

, for adult readers, topic knowledge is the primary determinant of cognitive interest in descriptive text, with the effect of topic knowledge on interest being strongest for readers knowing something about the topic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
readers who have some topic knowledge will be more likely to be motivated to read the text, which is a key element in learning from text.
the cognitive interest of a reader is a function of the reader’s topic knowledge.
readers’ prior topic knowledge is a key determinant of their cognitive interest, which in turn affects how well they will be able to learn from a text.
